column5: with the possibility of extension. Applicants must demonstrate a stable income from foreign clients or employers

column8: and relatively low cost of living
column9: Argentina has become an increasingly attractive destination for location-independent professionals.

column5: electronically-linked visa that allows citizens of eligible European and select other countries to visit Australia for tourism or business purposes. It permits multiple entries with stays of up to three months at a time

column8: is linked directly to the applicant's passport — meaning no physical visa label or stamp is required.

column4: Australia's Student Visa Subclass 500 allows international students to study full-time in a registered course at an Australian educational institution
column5: ranging from primary school to postgraduate level. Holders are permitted to work up to 48 hours per fortnight during term time
column6: with unlimited work rights during scheduled course breaks. The visa is granted for the duration of the enrolled course and can also include provisions for eligible family members to accompany the student to Australia.

column4: Australia's Working Holiday Visa Subclass 417 is designed for young people aged 18 to 30 (or up to 35 for citizens of certain countries) from eligible nations who wish to holiday and work in Australia for up to 12 months. Visa holders can work for any employer during their stay
column5: though they are limited to six months with the same employer
column6: and may extend their visa for a second or even third year by completing a specified number of days of regional work in designated industries such as agriculture
column8: or mining. It is one of Australia's most popular temporary visas
column9: offering a unique opportunity to explore the country while supplementing travel funds through employment.

column4: Australia's Temporary Graduate Visa Subclass 485 allows international students who have recently completed a qualification at an Australian institution to live
column6: and study in Australia on a temporary basis after graduation. The visa is divided into two streams — the Graduate Work stream
column7: for graduates with skills and qualifications in an occupation on a relevant skilled occupation list
column8: and the Post-Study Work stream
column9: for those who have completed a bachelor's degree or higher. Depending on the stream and the location of study
column10: the visa can be granted for between two and six years
column11: giving graduates valuable opportunities to gain Australian work experience after their studies.
